## Power takes most of the supply

These illustrative figures follow four energy sources through power generation and heating to the three places that use them. Each ribbon is as wide as its flow, and a node is as tall as the larger of what enters and leaves it.

```chart
type: sankey
title: Coal and gas feed most of the power that homes and industry use
subtitle: Energy flows in TWh, synthetic
data:
  inline:
    - {from: Coal, to: Power, twh: 35}
    - {from: Gas, to: Power, twh: 30}
    - {from: Gas, to: Heat, twh: 25}
    - {from: Wind, to: Power, twh: 20}
    - {from: Solar, to: Power, twh: 10}
    - {from: Power, to: Homes, twh: 45}
    - {from: Power, to: Industry, twh: 40}
    - {from: Power, to: Losses, twh: 10}
    - {from: Heat, to: Homes, twh: 15}
    - {from: Heat, to: Industry, twh: 10}
encoding: {source: from, target: to, y: twh}
axes:
  y: {label: TWh}
```

*Source: Illustrative values.*

Use the keyboard or pointer to read the size of each flow and node, and the share it takes of what leaves its source and what enters its target.
